EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows two strong bands in the 700–800 cm⁻¹ region (703 and 788 cm⁻¹), characteristic of C–Cl vibrations in chlorinated organics (consistent with halide bands near 792/765 cm⁻¹; GFQ-046). A strong band at 2251 cm⁻¹ is consistent with a high-frequency C≡C stretch of an internal alkyne; while GFQ-010 lists ~1700–2200 cm⁻¹, electron-withdrawing chloromethyl substituents can shift an internal alkyne toward the high end of this range. The absence of a ≡C–H stretch near ~3300 cm⁻¹ supports an internal (non-terminal) alkyne over candidate 5. CH stretches at 2962 and 3005 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-003) and CH bending at 1272/1433 cm⁻¹ match aliphatic groups in candidate 1. The 2340 cm⁻¹ band is plausibly ambient N₂ in Raman (GFQ-008), not a molecular feature requiring N or P in the candidate. Overall, ClCC#CCCl (1) best explains the halogen-region peaks, the internal alkyne, and the aliphatic CH features.
